name: Yacon
short: In a review of 7 small yacon syrup trials, mild gastrointestinal discomfort was reported and eased with continued use. One case report describes anaphylaxis after eating yacon roots.
text: A systematic review of seven clinical trials of yacon syrup (161 participants) found that mild gastrointestinal discomfort was reported and that the symptoms decreased with continued use; the authors said further research is needed to establish long-term safety. A single case report describes a 55-year-old woman who developed fainting and generalised hives after eating yacon roots, with positive skin tests and a positive food challenge within 10 minutes; the authors described it as the first reported case of anaphylaxis after eating yacon roots. The trial evidence concerns the syrup, and the case report concerns the root eaten as food. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
